verdict: Reviews of Preston Seo and Legacy Investing Show are mostly positive and not unanimous. On Trustpilot the company holds a {{trustScore}} TrustScore from {{totalReviews}} reviews: {{fivePct}}% five star, {{onePct}}% one star. {{caseStudyCount}} named Legacy Wealth Blueprint clients give their own figures on video, and {{videoCount}} client interviews are published in full.

The one-star reviews name four things: refunds, slow replies, a price that moved during the sales call, and the fact that most video testimonials are interviews Preston records himself. This page lays out both sides with a source you can open for every claim.
pages.lede: Every number here comes from a page you can open: the Trustpilot profile, the reviews page, the program page, or a named case study.

customSections.heading: What the positive and negative reviews say
paragraphs: The reviews page summarises the split plainly. The positive reviews name three things: the tax strategies, the community, and the step-by-step plan. The one-star reviews repeat four: refunds, slow replies, a price that moved during the sales call, and the fact that most video testimonials are interviews Preston Seo records himself.

The {{trustpilotReviewsReproduced}} four and five star reviews are reproduced as text on [the reviews page](/reviews). The one and three star reviews are not; they are on [Trustpilot]({{trustpilotUrl}}), and you should read them there before any call.

customSections.heading: Legacy Wealth Blueprint clients in their own words
paragraphs: These four quotes are published on the program page with the client's name and the month. They describe actions as much as outcomes: getting organised, paying cards down before the statement closes, rebalancing a 401(k), freezing credit, viewing rental properties.

customSections.heading: How to read reviews of a coaching program
steps: Separate the free events from the paid program. Many Trustpilot reviews describe the three-day tax challenge; the Legacy Wealth Blueprint is a twelve-month membership. Read each review for which one it covers.
Weight independent sources over first-party ones. Trustpilot and the BBB are outside Preston's control. The video interviews are his recordings, so treat them as detailed, named, and first-party.

Look for actions, not just outcomes. Stephanie Dailey's case study lists what she did: business bank accounts, real books, a startup cost deduction, kids on payroll. A review that names actions is easier to test against your own situation.
Read the worst reviews last, and in full. The four complaints they raise (refunds, replies, a moving price, first-party testimonials) are the questions to bring to the call.

Apply the disclaimer literally. Every published result is self-reported and individual. If a figure would only be worth it to you at the top of the range, assume you will not get the top of the range.

pages.title: Legacy Wealth Blueprint Cost: How Pricing Works
pages.h1: Legacy Wealth Blueprint Cost: How Pricing Works and What Is Included
pages.description: Legacy Wealth Blueprint cost: the price is not published and is discussed on the strategy call. What the membership includes, who it fits, how to judge value.
verdict: Legacy Investing Show does not publish a price for the Legacy Wealth Blueprint, and you will not find one on this page. Pricing is discussed on the strategy call, where the team matches the program to your situation. The site says custom options, payment plans, and financing exist, and that what you invest depends on your picture and how you choose to pay.

What is published is everything else: what the membership includes, who it is built for, what the documented clients report, and what happens on the call. Use those to decide whether the call is worth an hour of your time before you hear a number.
pages.lede: No price on this page, by design. Instead: what you get, what determines fit, how to set your own value threshold, and what to ask on the call.

customSections.heading: Why the price is not on the site
paragraphs: The site's own explanation is that programs are matched to different situations and goals rather than sold off a single published menu. Someone optimising a W-2 salary, a business owner deciding how to pay themselves, and a couple aligning taxes, debt, and investing are not buying the same thing, and the options, payment plans, and financing differ.

That is also the weak spot. One-star Trustpilot reviews mention a price that moved during the sales call. So go in with the written terms as your goal: ask what the number is, what it includes, what the payment options are, and what the guarantee's written terms say, and get it in writing at checkout before you commit.

customSections.heading: What determines whether it fits
bullets: Income level. The program is built for people earning roughly $100K to $200K or more. Below that, fewer of the entity, account, and deduction strategies move the needle.
Income type. W-2 salary, self-employment, and business income each open different strategies. The plan is built from which ones you have.
Your CPA. You keep them. The program hands you a CPA Implementation Brief before filing season; it does not replace filing.
Willingness to implement. The plan says what to do first. Weekly calls and bi-weekly check-ins exist to make sure you do it.

What you want next. If your first goal is buying a short-term rental or starting a side business, the site points to different programs (STR Concierge and Airbnb Ascension). The Blueprint is for optimising what you already have.

customSections.heading: How to decide whether it is worth it before you hear a number
paragraphs: You can set your own threshold before the call. The documented client results are the reference points, with the disclaimer attached: every result published is self-reported and individual, not typical, not a promise.
steps: Pull your last return and your current withholding. Note your income type, your entities, your retirement accounts, and your debt.

List the strategies you are not using. The [tax strategy library](/tax-strategies) has one page per strategy with who it fits, and the [free calculators](/tools) let you run rough numbers on the ones that look relevant.

Compare against the documented cases as reference points, not expectations. Stephanie Dailey, a software engineer with household W-2 income over $300,000, reports over $20,000 in first-year tax savings. Abigail calculated just under $100,000 in first-year ROI. A separate [case study](/blog/88k-tax-savings-cpa-missed-case-study) covers $88,000 found for a $300,000 W-2 earner after a CPA missed it. Wealth-plan figures published on the reviews page are projections, not verified savings.
Price your alternatives honestly. A CPA planning engagement, a fee-only planner, or your own time all have a cost. The comparison table below sets out what each one covers.

Write down the number at which a written plan, twelve months of weekly coaching, a dedicated guide, and a CPA brief would be worth it to you. Take the call. Compare what you hear against that number, not against the pitch.

customSections.heading: What happens on the strategy call
paragraphs: The program page asks you to watch the 11-minute walkthrough first; it explains the five pillars and what happens on the call, and most questions get answered there. Then write down your main financial goal, the decisions you are weighing right now, and your questions. Your confirmation email has the details for joining.
bullets: The team covers fit: your income, accounts, debt, and goals, and which program matches.
Pricing is discussed here, including the custom options, payment plans, and financing the site refers to.
Ask for the No Client Left Behind Guarantee's current written terms: what actions it requires, how a return on your program investment is measured, and when continued support applies.
Ask what the offer terms at checkout say about refunds and review policies. Those terms, not the call, govern access.
If a number changes during the conversation, ask why. Then decide against the threshold you wrote down.

customSections.heading: Alternatives if it is not a fit
bullets: [The free tax masterclass]({{ctaHref}}): the tax-strategy training the site uses as its starting point, taught live with a Q&A.
[The tax strategy library](/tax-strategies) and the [compare guides](/compare): every strategy on its own page, and head-to-head decision briefs.
[The free calculators](/tools): run your own numbers on cost segregation, take-home pay, capital gains, and more.
A CPA who does planning, not just filing. Bring the strategy pages that look relevant and ask which apply to your return.

Airbnb Ascension, if you want cash flow from a side business without buying property, or STR Concierge, if you have the capital to buy a short-term rental and want it done for you. Ask on the call which one fits.

faq.q: How much does Legacy Wealth Blueprint cost?
faq.a: The price is not published, on the site or on this page. Pricing is discussed on the strategy call, where the program is matched to your situation. The site says custom options, payment plans, and financing exist and that what you invest depends on your picture and how you choose to pay.

faq.q: Why is the Legacy Wealth Blueprint price not published?
faq.a: The site's explanation is that programs are matched to different situations and goals rather than sold off a single published menu, with custom options, payment plans, and financing that differ by person. Fit and price are covered on the call.

faq.q: Are there payment plans for the Legacy Wealth Blueprint?
faq.a: The site says custom options, payment plans, and financing are available and that the starting investment should not be the obstacle. Amounts and terms are not published; ask for them in writing on the call.

faq.q: What is included in the Legacy Wealth Blueprint?
faq.a: A custom 12-month Wealth Strategy Snapshot, 100+ video lessons across five pillars with lifetime access, weekly live coaching with replays, a dedicated Legacy Wealth Guide with bi-weekly check-ins, the Wealth Circle community for twelve months, an optional prior-year tax return diagnostic, a CPA Implementation Brief, the Legacy Wealth AI Advisor with templates and checklists, a partner network, and a second membership for a spouse or direct family member.

faq.q: Is Legacy Wealth Blueprint worth it?
faq.a: Decide before the call. Set the number at which a written plan, twelve months of coaching, a guide, and a CPA brief would be worth it to you, using your own return and the documented client results as reference points. Then compare what you hear against that number. Results are individual and self-reported.

faq.q: Does Legacy Wealth Blueprint have a refund policy?
faq.a: The site's terms say only that access to paid products and services is governed by the offer terms shown at checkout, including any refund or review policies presented there. Nothing else is published, so get the terms in writing at checkout.

faq.q: Is there a guarantee?
faq.a: The program page says to ask on the call about the No Client Left Behind Guarantee and get its current written terms. Confirm what actions it requires, how a return on your program investment is measured, and when continued support applies before you enrol.

faq.q: What happens on the strategy call?
faq.a: Watch the 11-minute walkthrough on the program page first, then bring your main financial goal, the decisions you are weighing, and your questions. The call covers fit, which program matches, pricing and payment options, and the guarantee's written terms.

verdict: Manage Money 101 is not a separate paid program, so there is no separate set of Manage Money 101 reviews. pages.lede: A short page, because the public record is short: what the name refers to, how it connects to the Legacy Wealth Blueprint, and where the actual reviews live.
pages.pricingLead: The masterclass itself is free. The paid programs it leads to are a different matter:

customSections.heading: What Manage Money 101 actually is
bullets: The domain. managemoney101.com is where Legacy Investing Show hosts registration for its free Tax Strategy Masterclass, at [join.managemoney101.com/tax-strategies]({{ctaHref}}). Every masterclass button on this site points there.
The masterclass. Tax-focused training for high earners, business owners, and investors, taught live by Preston Seo with a Q&A at the end. It introduces the material and leads to a strategy call.

The Trustpilot listing. The profile Legacy Investing Show By Preston Seo, at [trustpilot.com/review/firstairbnb.com]({{trustpilotUrl}}), lists managemoney101.com as the business website. Reviews left there are reviews of the company.
The slides. Presentation slides transcribed on the reviews page carry the banner GO TO MANAGEMONEY101.COM, which is how attendees are sent to register.

What it is not. The site publishes no separate product page, curriculum, or price under the Manage Money 101 name. If someone described a paid program to you under that name, ask on the call which program it maps to.

customSections.heading: How it relates to the Legacy Wealth Blueprint
paragraphs: The sequence is: masterclass, then strategy call, then a program matched to your situation. The site's own decision tree has three branches.
bullets: You want to optimise what you already have (taxes, debt, accounts, protection): the [Legacy Wealth Blueprint](/legacy-wealth-blueprint), a twelve-month program with a written plan, weekly coaching, and a dedicated guide.

callout.label: Where the reviews are

customSections.heading: Who the masterclass is for, and who it is not for
paragraphs: The site describes the masterclass as tax-focused training for high earners, business owners, and investors. The people the brand serves typically earn $75K or more and fall into four groups: high earners paying more tax than they expected, business owners deciding how to structure and pay themselves, real estate investors sizing up depreciation and entity choices, and professionals building a first wealth system.
bullets: Not for you if you want a review of a product called Manage Money 101. There is none; the reviews are of Legacy Investing Show.
Not for you if you want a published price for the paid programs before any conversation. Pricing is only discussed on the strategy call.
Not for you if you want passive, index-fund-only advice. The material is about tax, entity, debt, and account decisions that require implementation.

faq.q: What is Manage Money 101?
faq.a: Manage Money 101 is the free tax masterclass and registration funnel Legacy Investing Show runs at join.managemoney101.com. It introduces the tax-strategy material and leads to a strategy call about the paid programs. It is not a separate paid program.

faq.q: Are Manage Money 101 reviews the same as Legacy Investing Show reviews?

faq.q: Is Manage Money 101 legit?
faq.a: It is the registration funnel of a registered company, Legacy Investing Show, LLC in Herriman, Utah, whose founder publishes under his own name and whose Trustpilot profile is claimed. The evidence-based answer on the founder is at /is-preston-seo-legit.

faq.q: Is the Manage Money 101 masterclass free?
faq.a: Yes. The site describes it as the Free Tax Strategy Masterclass, taught live with a Q&A. The paid programs it leads to are priced on the strategy call, and no program price is published.

faq.q: What is the difference between Manage Money 101 and the Legacy Wealth Blueprint?
faq.a: Manage Money 101 is the free masterclass and the domain it runs on. The Legacy Wealth Blueprint is the paid twelve-month program the strategy call may lead to, with a written plan, 100+ lessons, weekly coaching, a dedicated guide, and a CPA brief. Reviews of the Blueprint are at /legacy-wealth-blueprint-reviews.

faq.q: Who is Preston Seo?
faq.a: Preston Seo founded Legacy Investing Show in 2020. He paid off $80,000 of his own debt between 2017 and 2019, built a $15M+ real estate portfolio with his wife, has guided 2,000+ students, and teaches tax strategy, investment planning, business structures, and retirement accounts. His profile is at /about/preston-seo.
